title: Browser tabs are closed by asking the agent that owns them, never silently
notes:
From the Rust review (/tmp/rust-review.md): 11 open project-browser tabs held about 517 MB. The user's rule: never close a tab just because it is idle; the agent responsible for it decides.

Each tab already has an owner (the session that opened or claimed it). Two triggers:
1. An agent ending: when its pane is released or finished, or its session ends, and it still owns open tabs, the app asks that agent first (a message naming the tabs: keep or close) and closes only those it lets go. A tab whose owner is gone with no answer is left open and listed, not closed.
2. Idle tabs: a tab that sees no browser_* call and no user input for 30 minutes (a setting) gets one question to its owning pane: may it be closed? Yes closes it; no or no answer keeps it, and it is not asked again until it has been used and gone idle again.

A tab the user opened or is looking at is never asked about. Decision modules with tests (who to ask, when the idle timer resets), the dashboard-browser skill and the browser docs updated.
